summary.title: Computer Networking Fundamentals
summary.one_liner: A short illustrated series that explains networking basics, mainly Ethernet and the data link layer (OSI L2), with hands-on labs for each topic.
takeaways: Ethernet broadcast domains: how L2 segments are bridged into one domain
How a single IP subnet can map to one or several L2 segments
How VLANs split one broadcast domain into smaller domains on a switch
The difference between bridges and switches, based on the author's data center tour
Plain-language introductions to iptables and SSH local and remote port forwarding
summary.summary: This learning series by iximiuz is a condensed, illustrated introduction to networking aimed at software engineers, focusing on wired Ethernet at OSI layer 2 with some neighboring-layer coverage. It contains an intro article on networking basics, plain-language guides to Linux iptables and SSH tunnels (local and remote port forwarding), and a comparison of bridges and switches. The series also has hands-on labs on Ethernet broadcast domains, mapping L3 subnets to L2 segments (with Proxy ARP mentioned as a follow-up), and simple VLAN configuration. The page is an index of these posts, and the labs are the practical part.
